text:
amy_support: FYI customer reported sudden 401 invalid_api_key across their app after we turned on org SSO group sync yesterday. They say key still shows as active in dashboard.

amy_support: Customer quote: \"calls start failing ~2026-03-14 21:00 UTC, nothing changed in app, same key. Dashboard shows key active, no rotations from customer side.\"

amy_support: They pasted a minimal repro curl:

amy_support: ```curl -i -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Authorization: Api-Key sk_live_ABCDEF123456' \
  -d '{\"model\":\"gpt-small\",\"prompt\":\"hi\",\"max_tokens\":5}'
```

juan_engineer: Can we check key metadata and audit events for that key_id? Ask customer for the masked key_id (first/last 4 chars) and org name.

amy_support: Sent request to customer for key_id and org. They responded: key id mask sk_live_****3456, org acme-corp.

juan_engineer: Looking in internal logs for that mask... :eyes:

deploy-bot: policy.event: \"sso_group_sync\" triggered for org=acme-corp by admin_id=U345, action=apply_security_policies

juan_engineer: I see an automated policy enforcement at 2026-03-14T20:58:03Z: policy \"restrict-token-lifetime\" applied to acme-corp -> flagged existing long-lived keys for review. One key marked \"disallowed_by_policy\" and auto-disabled by policy engine. That will return 401 even if dashboard still shows active (dashboard sync lag).

amy_support: Customer says dashboard shows active. Is that a UI eventual-consistency thing? Can we provide immediate remediation steps?

sre_oncall: UI sync lag known in cases where policy engine toggles flags. We can either re-enable the key or recommend short-lived token flow. For now re-enable and advise rotating to an org-managed service key tied to SSO.

juan_engineer: Re-enabled the key in the policy service (policy_id=pol-78). Confirmed internal status=enabled now. Tell customer to retry and also try an explicit HEAD to key status endpoint.

amy_support: Sent: "We re-enabled the key on our side — please retry the same curl. If still 401, do a request to: \n\ncurl -s -H 'Authorization: Api-Key sk_live_ABCDEF123456' https://api.redwood.ai/v1/keys/status\n\nand paste the JSON response."

amy_support: Customer replied: "after your re-enable it's green again, calls succeed. Thanks. But can you explain why it was auto-disabled?"

juan_engineer: Summary for customer: after enabling SSO group sync, org-wide security policy \"enforce-ephemeral-keys\" was applied. It flagged long-lived keys and auto-disabled ones that matched the rule. Dashboard display had a small lag before reflecting the policy change. Recommend creating an org-scoped service key or switching to short-lived tokens via our OAuth flow. Documented mitigation linked: https://docs.redwood.ai/security/keys#sso-policies

jordan_account: I'll follow up with the customer to help with migration and offer a staged rollout plan so they don't hit auto-disable during group sync.

amy_support: Customer confirmed they'll rotate and try the managed flow next week. Closing thread after follow-up scheduled.

amy_support: Notes -> internal ticket created INF-3421, tag=sso-policy, action=recommend rotation, owner=jordan_account
